content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 26. Supplemental: SEI tradeoff analysis concepts. This unit focuses on performance scenarios and budgets.
Performance architecture starts with scenarios and budgets. Latency, throughput, jitter, resource use, and user-perceived responsiveness must be tied to realistic workloads and environments.
A performance budget allocates responsibility across architecture elements. Without a budget, teams may optimize locally while the end-to-end path still fails.
Studio: create an end-to-end latency budget for a search request across client, API, service, cache, database, and network hops.

concepts.name: Performance scenario
concepts.description: A quality scenario that specifies workload, environment, response, and measurable performance target.

concepts.name: Latency budget
concepts.description: An allocation of acceptable response time across elements in an end-to-end path.

concepts.name: Throughput
concepts.description: The amount of work a system can complete in a given period under specified conditions.

concepts.name: Workload model
concepts.description: A description of expected requests, users, data size, arrival patterns, and operating conditions.
